citation: Retrospective study, Tianjin First Central Hospital: mNGS vs traditional methods in haematological malignancy patients with febrile neutropenia after empiric antibiotics, 2022
study_design: Retrospective cohort (mNGS vs traditional microbiology; diagnostic efficiency vs clinical diagnosis)

population.population_description: 192 haematological malignancy patients on empiric antibiotics with persistent fever after 72–96 h; 102 FN, 90 non-FN; clinical diagnosis: infected 145 (75.52%), non-infected 22 (11.46%), uncertain 24 (12.50%); 68 (35.42%) had transplantation or CAR-T; specimens: blood 157, BALF 11, tissue 9, body fluid 8, pus 5, sputum 2

neutropenic_status: FN defined as absolute neutrophil count (ANC) <0.5 × 10^9/L; non-FN ANC >0.5 × 10^9/L

index_test.platform_or_panel: BGISEQ-100 gene sequencer; DNA extracted with TIANamp Micro DNA kit, RNA with QIAamp Viral RNA Mini kit, reverse-transcribed to ds cDNA; NCBI-derived reference databases with negative controls

reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis adjudicated from clinical manifestations, traditional laboratory results, imaging and microbiological evidence; patients divided into infected (145), non-infected (22) and uncertain (24) groups

comparator_2x2.against: clinical diagnosis as reference (FN group, n=102; infected n=75, non-infected n=12); mNGS sensitivity 88.00%, specificity 58.33%, PPV 92.96%, NPV 56.25% (traditional: sens 29.33%, spec 100%, PPV 100%, NPV 18.46%). TP/FN/TN/FP back-derived: 66/75=88.00%, 7/12=58.33%, PPV 66/71=92.96%

diagnostic_yield.basis: mNGS-positive in 154/192 (80.21%) vs traditional 48/192 (25.00%), P<0.001; bacteria 93 (48.44%), fungus 44 (22.92%), virus 81 (42.19%); mixed infection 61 (39.61%) vs 4.17%; 141 pathogen species vs 15 by traditional methods

additional_yield_vs_conventional: both methods positive in 48 (25%) cases; among these 31/48 partly matched, 10/48 fully matched, 7/48 mismatched; FN subgroup: empiric antibiotics of 46/102 (45.10%) patients did not cover all mNGS-detected pathogens
turnaround_time: Results typically came back within 24 hours; samples sent to GBI laboratory within 12 h
therapy_change: After adjusting the antimicrobial regimen according to mNGS results, effective rate at 72 h was 22/46 (47.83%) and at 7 days 24/102 (52.17%); 5 patients discontinued inappropriate antibiotics without adverse prognosis

quality_flags.overlap_risk: clinical diagnosis partly incorporates mNGS results; uncertain group (n=24) excluded from accuracy calculations — denominator ambiguity; 2x2 derived, not verbatim

quadas2_notes: Retrospective, single centre, mixed specimen types (mainly blood). Sensitivity/specificity reported per FN and non-FN subgroups vs clinical diagnosis; non-FN mNGS sens 81.42%, spec 63.64%. Derived 2x2 flagged; PPV/NPV verbatim. Fungal diagnosis in FN: 21/33 (63.63%) diagnosed with fungal infection.

evidence_quotes.quote: We retrospectively analyzed 192 patients who have received empiric antibiotic treatment. They were diagnosed with hematological malignancies in Tianjin First Central Hospital, Tianjin, China, between January 2019 and July 2021. A total of 102 patients were FN, and the remaining 90 patients were non-FN who did not develop neutropenia but had a fever.
FN patients needed to meet: absolute neutrophil count (ANC) in peripheral blood <0.5 × 10 9 /L.

the pathogen detection rate of mNGS was significantly higher than the traditional method (80.21% vs 25.00%, P <0.001). And it has obvious advantages in detecting mixed pathogens infection (80.21% vs 4.17%, P <0.001).

evidence_quotes.section: Table 3 Diagnostic Efficiency of Culture and mNGS Compared to Clinical Diagnosis

evidence_quotes.quote: according to clinical diagnosis, all patients were divided into the infected group (145 cases, 75.52%), the non-infected group (22 cases, 11.46%), and the uncertain (24 cases,12.50%).

(Sensitivity=mNGS-positive/clinical diagnosed infections. Specificity=mNGS-negative/clinical diagnosed non-infections. PPV= clinical diagnosed infections with mNGS-positive/mNGS-positive. NPV= clinical diagnosed non-infections with mNGS-negative/ mNGS-negative.)

In the FN group, empiric antibiotic treatment of 46/102 (45.10%) patients did not treat all the pathogens detected by mNGS. After adjusting the antimicrobial regimen according to the results of mNGS, the effective rate at 72 hours and 7 days was 22/46 (47.83%) and 24/102 (52.17%), respectively.
those samples were collected and the results typically came back within 24 hours, which could help clinicians adjust antibiotics in time.
